prompt: Write the career advice post you wish someone had handed you as a young software engineer fresh out of college: the stuff about how the industry and business actually work that no CS degree or career center covers. Be blunt and practical.

I run a company with a big, ugly legacy codebase, and everyone keeps saying we should rewrite it all in whatever framework is fashionable. Write a candid first-person post from someone who tried a big rewrite and what they concluded about it.

You've spent about five years researching one niche topic outside academia, funded by a foundation, then a job at the company at the center of it, then a research role, and you're about to finish a book. Friends keep saying it was basically a PhD. Write a reflective essay on how you actually did it, phase by phase, what you'd tell someone considering independent research instead of a doctorate, and how the PhD itself might be reimagined.
What would the best possible essay be like? Take that question seriously and follow it wherever it leads, including into how essays actually get written.

I'm a psychiatry resident and I've been poking around online drug-review sites, where patients rate their medications. Write a blog post about what you might learn by comparing patient ratings with doctors' ratings and with how often drugs get prescribed. Be honest about what could be confounding the numbers.

I keep seeing arguments of the form 'group X doesn't REALLY believe what they say, they just want Y' in politics, with abortion as the standard example. Write a long essay on why that style of argument is so tempting and why it usually fails. You can be pro-choice and still take the other side seriously.

I keep noticing that practices that horrify new hires at tech companies are treated as completely normal by everyone who's been there a while. Write an essay about why this happens in software organizations, what other fields have learned about it, and what it would take to change it.

Two well-designed experiments on whether academic hiring committees favor men or women just came out with opposite results, and each side is citing its own. How should a sensible person think about that? Write it as a blog post, and be willing to speculate about why the studies differ.

After an election loss, everyone says the losing party should be more emotional, more tribal, less wonky. Write an essay about the hidden risk in that advice: what happens to a party's own thinking when it adopts the style that wins votes?
There's tons of advice for founders but hardly any on being a good startup investor. Write a practical essay on how to do it well, from someone who's invested in a lot of companies.
I'm a parent of a young child and I've been thinking about whether the things we do for our kids are truly selfless. Write an essay on that, from your own experience.

People keep asking me whether open source maintainers could get paid if projects just switched to commercial or more restrictive licenses. I'm skeptical but haven't put my reasons in order. Write a short blog post laying out the case, both practical and philosophical.
Is there any good evidence for lost advanced civilizations from before the end of the last Ice Age? Write a skeptical but fair essay weighing the case, and end with some probabilities.

Blog post idea: what are the different kinds of knowledge you need to be good at debugging, and what can a programmer actually do to get better at each? Feel free to draw on research about how people troubleshoot.
Write a piece on why the phrase 'no evidence' is so slippery in science and journalism. Does it have any consistent meaning, and what should a careful writer say instead?

Write a personal essay about your heroes: the people (and maybe things) whose example actually shapes how you decide what to do. Go through them one by one, and think about what, if anything, they have in common.

You run a small educational DNS playground website whose hand-rolled DNS server had lots of correctness bugs, and you just rebuilt it on top of PowerDNS. Write a blog post about the migration and the challenges you ran into along the way.
Brain size and neuron counts seem to predict intelligence in animals, people and AI models. But why should that be? Neurons aren't storage for solving a puzzle in a minute. Think it through for me.

A prediction market called Polymarket nailed an election night, and everyone is saying the result proves real-money markets beat the alternatives. I'm not so sure that follows. Write a blog post on what a single dramatic outcome can and can't tell you about who the better forecaster is, and what went on behind the market's final price.

I want a blog post about a self-experiment: I tried a sleep supplement, thought it was working wonders, then ran a proper blinded trial on myself to check. Write it as the experimenter, including what went wrong with my first impression and what I actually learned.
Write a book review of Scott Rosenberg's Dreaming in Code, about the Chandler project, that uses it to talk about why ambitious software projects fail to converge. Open with something unexpected.

I studied computer science and then went to art school, and people keep asking me why. Write an essay arguing that programming is closer to painting than to science or engineering, and what follows from that for how hackers should work and make a living.

A friend swears by 'training your inner pigeon', using behaviorism on yourself by rewarding yourself when you do what you want to do more of. Does that actually work? Think it through skeptically, using what you know about conditioning.
You worked at Yahoo in the late 90s after they acquired your startup. Write an essay about what actually went wrong there, and what lessons today's software companies should take from it.

Every time a big tech company comes up online, someone says 'what do all those thousands of engineers even do? I could build that in a weekend.' Write a blog post on why that intuition is wrong (or whether it is).
Why are listicles ('7 things...', '10 ways...') so popular? I'd like a proper essay on the format: what it does for readers and writers, and what it costs.

I keep running into the claim that people who believe effort matters more than ability do better in life, and the studies behind it look impressive. I'm instinctively skeptical but can't say why. Write an honest, wide-ranging essay on the growth mindset research that admits your biases and takes the evidence seriously.

I'm a teacher and I'm tired of hearing that schools are obsolete and that we should just personalize everything. Write a long essay arguing for a more sympathetic, skeptical-of-reformers account of why school looks the way it does: why classrooms are grouped by age, why so much of it seems inefficient, and what we'd need to understand before changing it.

Could parasites that hijack animal behavior have shaped how our brains and bodies work, including why psychiatric drugs so often stop working? Walk me through a recent academic paper on this, how plausible it is, and what it would mean for biology if true.

People say the Church never burned scientists for their science, only for heresy. Suppose that's true. Is there still something to learn from it about what happens to curious people under an orthodoxy, and what a sensible person should do about it? Write an essay, and feel free to range from medieval Europe to the Soviet Union.
You run a small software company. Tell the story of a time you realized you'd approved something and then forgot you had, and what that says about how managers should treat their own advice.
Write a first-person story about a costly mistake a founder made in the early days of a small business by not paying attention to paperwork and structure.

Should news organizations spend so much energy debunking stupid or fringe ideas? Write an essay weighing the case for challenging them against the case for ignoring them, ideally using a historical example that tells us something.

My apartment is full of things I picked up because they were cheap or free, and I can't seem to stop. Write me a personal essay about our relationship to stuff: why we accumulate it, what it actually costs us, and whether our attitudes have kept up with how cheap things have become.
Why do non-technical managers and customers misjudge how far along a software project is? Write an essay for programmers on how to communicate with them.

A few years ago you did a rough cost-benefit analysis of marijuana legalization and ended up undecided. Now several states have legalized and data is coming in. Write the follow-up, honestly, including where your earlier prediction turned out wrong.

I keep hearing that effective charity just means measuring outcomes with good data. Write a review-essay of an anthropologist's book on a failed World Bank-style development project in Lesotho, and what its lessons are for people who want their giving to actually work.
Write an essay on why becoming a really proficient programmer keeps getting harder even as tools get better, and what that means for hiring and for picking technology for a new project.

You've spent a career on performance work (CPU microcode, search indexes) and lately you've been pointing coding agents at optimization problems: a regex engine, a board game AI, your own ripgrep usage. Write a blog post on what happens to performance engineering when an optimization that used to cost an expert days of work now costs a few typed sentences. Draw on your own experiments, and keep it informal.

Groups like nations, religions, fandoms, parties and online communities all seem to share some common machinery, whatever they claim to be about. Write an essay on what that shared thing is, why people value belonging to these groups despite the obvious dangers, and why almost any shared activity seems to drift toward becoming a social club.

A critic says the case for funding existential-risk work depends on made-up probabilities that you can shrink by adding zeroes until the argument fails. Write a response on when it is legitimate to put tiny numbers on things and why the zeroes aren't free.

Open source software and blogging both seem to beat paid professionals at their own game. Write an essay on what the forces behind them should teach businesses about work, offices, and how companies are organized.

A new paper by AI researchers and philosophers tries to identify indicators of consciousness in AI systems. Write a thoughtful, skeptical but fair essay about what such work can and can't tell us, and how people will actually end up treating AIs.
Write a provocative piece arguing for the opposite of 'follow your heart': that you should pick one rulebook and obey it. Short, blunt lines.

I'm a medical student and our communication-skills classes feel strangely fake: role-plays, checklists, scripted phrases. Write me a thoughtful essay on whether you can teach doctors empathy, and what the difference is between seeming empathetic and actually being so.

I write technical explanations and try to keep the language simple, but I worry it sometimes reads as talking down to people. Write a blog post on how to explain complicated technical topics in plain language without sounding condescending.

Startups keep telling engineers their offers are worth more in expectation than a big-company package because of the equity. If that's true, why don't they just sell those options to investors and pay cash? Write an essay working through the cynical and non-cynical reasons companies prefer paying in options, and what it means for employees deciding between offers.

I've been getting defensive online lately and a friend asked why. Write a candid piece explaining, from the gut, why criticism that aims to make a group disreputable can doom it, and why that makes someone jumpy.

Is moral offsetting okay? Like flying and then paying to clean up the carbon, or eating meat and donating to an animal charity. Most people think that works for emissions but obviously not for murder. Write an essay trying to find a principled line instead of just saying 'trivial vs serious.'

Write an essay about why the causes that campaign hardest for attention so often seem to sabotage themselves, picking the most divisive examples to rally around. Use a few contemporary cases, and think about what incentives the media and the activists are each responding to.
I run a small software company and our projects always seem to drag. Write an essay applying ideas from manufacturing to how software teams work, and what to do about it.
Write a short blog post about the gap between how effortless great performances look and how much work lies behind them, and whether it matters if the audience ever finds out.

Write a thorough review of Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century for a smart reader who is not an economist and won't read the book. Cover what the data say, what you found convincing or confusing, and what could be done about it.
You've watched thousands of would-be founders ask where startup ideas come from. Write a blog post answering that properly.

Someone online argues that vitamin D studies show nothing only because they use tiny doses compared with what our ancestors got from sunlight. I tend to think vitamin D is mostly a bone chemical, but I want to be fair to that argument. Write a long, careful essay that checks the dosing claim against the actual numbers and says what a sensible person should conclude about supplements.
Write an essay about what it means for a programmer to really have a program loaded in their head, what helps or hurts that state, and what it implies about how companies organize software work.

People often argue that fear of new technology has historically done more harm than the technology itself (nuclear power being the classic case), and so we shouldn't be too cautious about AI. Is that argument right? Write an essay on how to think about it.

I just finished reading a book about bee cognition and I can't stop wondering: are bees actually smart? Write a funny but serious review-style essay that works through what we know about bee behaviour and where the line between instinct and real thinking might lie.

A magazine article says polyamory has a problem because black people are underrepresented in it. Write a response from someone in the poly community, thinking about why any group might be demographically skewed and what the framing does.

I just finished a big political biography and realized my school-taught picture of how power works is basically a cartoon. Write an essay on how real political operators actually accumulate power, and what that implies for the rest of us.

In what situations does teaching technical topics with comics actually help, and is 'some people are visual learners' a good enough answer? Write a reflective blog post from the perspective of someone who makes programming zines.

I keep hearing the Frankfurt School blamed for everything, and I also keep hearing that you're not allowed to say anything about them, and I honestly have no idea what they believed. I'm going to read one standard history of the group. Write me a skeptical, funny, honest guide to what these people were actually trying to say, using analogies an outsider can follow.
Write a creepy but informative blog post about the strangest and scariest sleep disorders, written by a medical trainee who has just read a sleep medicine textbook.

We were all raised on 'you get out what you put in.' I'm increasingly convinced that's false and that rewards for performance are wildly nonlinear in most areas that matter. Write an essay on where these outsized returns come from and what an ambitious person should do about it.
I'm a college senior about to start interviewing for jobs. Give me some honest advice about the pressure tactics recruiters use on students when making offers, and how to handle them.
Make the case for living entirely in the present and doing whatever you want right now. Write it as a short, confident essay on how to live.

Write a blog post in which you admit you were wrong about distributed version control like Mercurial and Git. Explain what finally made you understand why it matters, in terms someone who only knows Subversion could follow.
